candidates.original_title: Interval likelihood ratios: Applications for gated screening in schools
candidates.description: Using interval likelihood ratios to estimate post-test probabilities of math risk in a gated screening framework with middle school students.
candidates.citation_sentence: In the current study, we sought to replicate our initial evaluation of using interval LRs to estimate post-test probabilities to determine math risk (Klingbeil et al., 2019).
candidates.notes: Authors explicitly call this a 'direct replication' and the Discussion confirms the findings corroborate the original study's results.

candidates.original_title: Interval likelihood ratios: Applications for gated screening in schools
candidates.description: Using interval likelihood ratios rather than dichotomized likelihood ratios improves the efficiency and diagnostic accuracy of a gated screening framework for identifying math risk among middle school students.
candidates.citation_sentence: Klingbeil et al. (2019) conducted an initial evaluation of whether using interval LRs improved upon the diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of a gated screening framework but the LRs were applied to the same sample from which they were derived.
candidates.notes: The replication found support for reduced further assessment after the first screening step and similar diagnostic accuracy, but results diverged from the original after later screening steps, particularly in Grades 6 and 7.
